crime: Every morning her mother looked her over at the front door and sent her back: "Something's not right. Go fix it." She searched the hall mirror until she was late, and never found what was wrong.
In her cell, {WITCH_NAME} held up a hand mirror each morning and named aloud every flaw her Magic showed her. If she found it first, no one could send her back.

Another prisoner had once got four little sisters ready for school each morning. Here, at six, she walked the cell corridor straightening every girl's collar bow, held up her little mirror and said, "There." At {WITCH_NAME}'s door she walked on; there was nothing left to fix.
One morning she reached behind {WITCH_NAME} and straightened the bow at her nape, the one spot her hand mirror never showed. "You missed one. There."

{WITCH_NAME} asked her to the lake shore alone at dusk: "Fix my bow where no one will see." As the girl stood behind her retying it, {WITCH_NAME} turned, seized her by the cardigan and held her face down in the shallows until she was still.

Then she wrote a note in the girl's hand, listing every flaw her Magic found in the drowned body, and checked it stroke by stroke until her Magic found nothing wrong. She left it on the bank under the girl's shoes.

The prisoners found the girl face down in the shallows, her shoes on the bank over a note in her own hand that listed her flaws and ended, "I'm sorry." In the trial court, the prisoners ruled she had walked into the lake herself.

A prisoner held up a button picked from the stones under the water where the girl lay, and set it against one line of the note: "The second button of my cardigan, gone." It had come off in the water. The note was written over her drowned body, by eyes that see at a glance what is missing, in a hand without one wrong stroke.
fields.epitaph: The one time someone else found her flaw first, it was only to set it straight.
fields.epithet: The First to Find Her Own Flaws
execution: A giant hand mirror rose before her face, and a giant collar ribbon tied itself in a loose bow at her nape. She stood shackled, facing the mirror, her back to the court.
The ribbon drew its two loops out level to either side, cinching the bow tight around her throat.
In the mirror she clawed at the ribbon at her throat. Her hands never reached the bow behind her.
She sagged still against the ribbon. At her nape, a perfectly straight bow faced the court.

magic.name: Faultfinder
magic.text: At a glance, she sees exactly what is wrong, missing or out of place in anyone or anything.
